occurrences.source_excerpt: Compound fracture a fracture with an open wound/ skin breaks near the site of broken bone. Usually caused by a fragment of bone breaking through the skin during injury. With broken skin, risk of infection due to bacteria & other contaminants entering wound. Early treatment focuses on preventing infection The wound, tissues & bone must be cleaned out in surgical procedures as soon as possible. Fractured bone would be stabilized with a surgical procedure to allow wound healing.

occurrences.source_excerpt: Compound fracture a fracture with an open wound/ skin breaks near the site of broken bone. Usually caused by a fragment of bone breaking through the skin during injury. With broken skin, risk of infection due to bacteria & other contaminants entering wound. Early treatment focuses on preventing infection The wound, tissues & bone must be cleaned out in surgical procedures as soon as possible. Fractured bone would be stabilized with a surgical procedure to allow wound healing.

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 2 - Bone problems: osteoporosis, fracture and amputation

occurrences.source_excerpt: Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 2 - Bone problems: osteoporosis, fracture and amputation

occurrences.source_excerpt: Osteoporosis & Bone Remodeling • Bone remodeling - continuous process throughout life to maintaining bone strength and repairing micro-damage • Osteoporosis is the imbalance between bone resorption (breakdown) by osteoclasts and bone formation (building) by osteoblasts, leading to a net bone loss (Chang et al, 2019) 12/9/2025

Osteoporosis, benign • bone tumour, cancer 12/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Osteoporosis & Bone Remodeling • Bone remodeling - continuous process throughout life to maintaining bone strength and repairing micro-damage • Osteoporosis is the imbalance between bone resorption (breakdown) by osteoclasts and bone formation (building) by osteoblasts, leading to a net bone loss (Chang et al, 2019) 12/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Compound fracture a fracture with an open wound/ skin breaks near the site of broken bone. Usually caused by a fragment of bone breaking through the skin during injury. With broken skin, risk of infection due to bacteria & other contaminants entering wound. Early treatment focuses on preventing infection The wound, tissues & bone must be cleaned out in surgical procedures as soon as possible. Fractured bone would be stabilized with a surgical procedure to allow wound healing.

occurrences.source_excerpt: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) • Relative uncommon rheumatic disease that affect the spine • Prevalence: • Global – 0.1-1.4% [Dean et al, 2014] [Dean et al, 2014] • Hong Kong – 0.2-0.3% [Zhu et al, 2008] [Zhu et al, 2008] • long-term condition related to autoimmune disease • Joints and ligaments of spine and other areas of the body become • inflamed • e.g. sacroiliac joint, hips, • shoulders • May involve other organs such as eyes, lungs, heart 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) Causes: • no known cause • link with a particular gene variant known as HLA-B27 Risk factors: • Family history and genetics • Age (usually symptoms develop before age 45) • Biological gender: male • Autoimmune disease: psoriasis, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis 1/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) Treatment: • No cure for AS, treatment • available to relieve the symptoms and delay • progression • Medications to reduce pain & • inflammation: • NSAIDS • DMARDs, Biologics • Corticosteriods • Exercises: reduce pain & • stiffness • Physiotherapy: improve posture, • flexibility, joint mobility • Surgery: for rare cases to repair significantly damaged joints or correct severe bends in spine 1/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) • provides a standard language for classifying • body functions and structures, activities, participation levels & conditions in the world around us that influence health • classify health & health related • domains- assess health, functioning, activities & environmentalfactors • framework of the World Health • Organization (WHO) for measuring health and disability at both individuals and population levels

source_pages.document_title: Tutorial 1 - ICF

occurrences.source_excerpt: Dimensions of ICF • Disease: a known or identifiable cause, such as a virus, bacteria, genetic mutation, or other biological malfunction • Personal factors: gender, age, coping styles, social background, education, experience, characters… • Environmental factors: external physical/social factors (e.g. stairs, slopes, caregiver, employer, etc. •

source_pages.document_title: Tutorial 1 - ICF

occurrences.source_excerpt: Dimensions of ICF Body functions: physiological functions Activities: is the execution of a task or of body systems, including psychological action by an individual (e.g. self care, functions (e.g. sensory functions, mobility, communication) speech functions) Participation: involvement in a life Body structures: anatomical parts of the situation (e.g. employment, go to body, such as organ & limbs (e.g. eye, church, social gathering) ear, nerve, bones, muscles)

source_pages.document_title: Tutorial 1 - ICF

occurrences.source_excerpt: Short-term goals corresponds to body function & structure in ICF (impairment level) able to improve/manage in relatively shorter period • e.g. decrease pain at low back • e.g. decrease swelling at right knee • e.g. improve active range of motion at left shoulder

source_pages.document_title: Tutorial 1 - ICF

occurrences.source_excerpt: Long-term goals corresponds to activity/participation in ICF (functional level) need relatively longer period to achieve • E.g. independence in dressing/ bathing • E.g. able to walk with stick independently

occurrences.source_excerpt: Common signs & symptoms Joint swelling, pain, ➢ stiffness & decreased range of motion (ROM) ➢ may last for years, ➢ progress/get worse with ➢ time ➢ mild, moderate or severe ➢ may result in chronic pain, ➢ inability to do daily activities, difficulty in walking (both level ground / stairs) 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Signs & symptoms – Joints • Joint pain, tenderness, swelling, redness or stiffness > 6 weeks • Morning stiffness for > 1 hour • > ONE joint are affected • Small joints are commonly • affected – Hands, Wrists & toes • Symmetrical joint pain: on both sides of the body • Decrease joint range of • motion (ROM) • Joint deformity Flare - a period of high disease activity, last for days/months ** increases in inflammation & other symptoms 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Principles of Rehabilitation • Reduce/control inflammation • Manage symptoms such as pain, • stiffness & swelling • Maintain joint ROM • Joint protection strategies • Sufficient exercise for • maintenance of overall well- being: recommended 30-60 mins on 5 days/week with moderate intensity and exercise in water to reduce joint stress • Use of assistive device, e.g. orthosis to decrease pain, • prevent joint deformity • Prevent long term complications • Facilitate independency in ADLs 1/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Compound fracture a fracture with an open wound/ skin breaks near the site of broken bone. Usually caused by a fragment of bone breaking through the skin during injury. Fractured bone would be stabilized with a surgical procedure to allow wound healing.

occurrences.source_excerpt: Compound fracture a fracture with an open wound/ skin breaks near the site of broken bone. Usually caused by a fragment of bone breaking through the skin during injury. With broken skin, risk of infection due to bacteria & other contaminants entering wound. Fractured bone would be stabilized with a surgical procedure to allow wound healing.

occurrences.source_excerpt: Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 1: Minor • slight damage to cartilage +/- • osteophytes • NO apparent narrowing of joint space • (normal at X-ray) • Asymptomatic (NO pain / discomfort) Stage 2: Mild • some symptoms noted like • joint stiffness & pain, esp. after prolonged sitting • X-ray:clearly shown growth • of osteophytes, cartilage begin to get thin 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 4: Severe • further joint space • narrowing, with continuous cartilage loss • more significant pain & discomfort with daily activities due to joint • friction • X-ray: bone on bone • (cartilage completely worn / little left) • Deformity with varus (bow leg) or valgus (knock knee) 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) • Chronic inflammatory autoimmune • systemic disease • Chronic – long term • Inflammatory – joint • inflammation, thickening of synovium, leading to swelling, pain, +/- redness & warmth in • joints • Autoimmune – immune system mistakenly attacks the joints • Systemic – affects entire body / multiple organ systems • Damage cartilage, bones & joints • loss of cartilage, and narrow joint spacing loose, unstable joints with deformity 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) • Recommend early • diagnosis with aggressive treatment • most commonly affects joints of the hands, feet, wrists, elbows, knees and ankles • usually symmetrical • Can affect body systems, • such as skin, eyes, cardiovascular or respiratory systems • Can cause long-term • disability, pain & premature death 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Signs & symptoms – Joints • Joint pain, tenderness, swelling, redness or stiffness > 6 weeks • Morning stiffness for > 1 hour • > ONE joint are affected • Small joints are commonly • affected – Hands, Wrists & toes • Symmetrical joint pain: on both sides of the body • Decrease joint range of • motion (ROM) • Joint deformity Flare - a period of high disease activity, last for days/months ** increases in inflammation & other symptoms 1/9/2025

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Signs & symptoms – organs & body systems • Whole body: fatigue, loss of appetite & low-grade fever • Lungs: chest pain, shortness of breath (SOB), persistent cough - • inflammation & scarring • Heart: chest pain - inflammation of • tissue around the heart • Eyes: dryness, pain, redness • Blood vessels: affect blood flow • Skin: rheumatoid nodules – small lumps under the skin over bony • areas • Nerve: numbness, tingling, pain, • weakness • Blood: anaemia, low RBC • Bone: Osteoporosis • Mouth: dr

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 1 - Joint problems: osteoarthritis, rheumatology, ankylosing spondylitis and joint replacement

occurrences.source_excerpt: Principles of Rehabilitation • Reduce/control inflammation • Manage symptoms such as pain, • stiffness & swelling • Maintain joint ROM • Joint protection strategies • Sufficient exercise for • maintenance of overall well- being: recommended 30-60 mins on 5 days/week with moderate intensity and exercise in water to reduce joint stress • Use of assistive device, e.g. orthosis to decrease pain, • prevent joint deformity • Prevent long term complications • Facilitate independency in ADLs 1/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Signs & symptoms • Symptoms tend to develop gradually (over several months or years) • Morning stiffness > 30 min • Symptoms may come and go over time (flare) • Varies in symptoms, including pain, stiffness & swelling over back, sacroiliac joint, hips and • shoulders • extreme tiredness (fatigue) • For severe cases, vertebrae fuse together lead to rigid spine 1/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) Treatment: • No cure for AS, treatment • available to relieve the symptoms and delay • progression • Medications to reduce pain & • inflammation: • NSAIDS • DMARDs, Biologics • Corticosteriods • Exercises: reduce pain & • stiffness • Physiotherapy: improve posture, • flexibility, joint mobility • Surgery: for rare cases to repair significantly damaged joints or correct severe bends in spine 1/9/2025

occurrences.source_excerpt: Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025
